title: South Korea AI Basic Act: High-Impact Duties After 22 January 2026 Commencement
hook: Eight months after commencement (22 January 2026), September 2026 is the first full supervisory year for high-impact AI operators under the Korea AI Basic Act
answer_first: South Korea Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of Trust (the AI Basic Act) took effect on 22 January 2026. It is a promotion-plus-trust statute: it funds AI development while imposing safety, transparency, and human-oversight duties on operators of high-impact AI systems (systems that can significantly affect life, rights, or safety). Operators must notify the competent authority, implement risk-management measures, and provide user-facing notice when AI is in use. The Ministry of Science and ICT is the lead authority, with the Korea Communications Commission and Personal Information Protection Commission holding adjacent duties on communications and personal data. Unlike the EU AI Act, the Korean statute does not copy Annex-III high-risk lists or Article 5 prohibitions; it uses a high-impact designation and administrative guidance. As of 16 September 2026, buyers and deployers should treat Korean high-impact notification, user notice, and risk-management artefacts as first-year evidence — a verified measurement credential against those duties, under monitored containment, not provable isolation. UK-sovereign operators selling into Korea still need local counsel for designation scope.
council_positioning: Monitored containment, not provable isolation. Verified measurement credential. UK-sovereign, AUKUS-compatible.
sources: Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of Trust (Korea) — commenced 22 January 2026
